user.title: TP-Link Switch (SNMP)
user.description: Address and SNMP version of the switch. SNMP must be switched on at the switch.

data_description.host: IP address or name of the switch.
data_description.port: UDP port of the SNMP service, normally 161.
data_description.version: v2c fits most switches; v3 is encrypted, v1 is only for very old devices.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure switch
reconfigure.description: New address, version or credentials for {title}. The same switch must answer.

data_description.host: IP address or name of the switch.
data_description.port: UDP port of the SNMP service, normally 161.
data_description.version: The SNMP version; when you change it, the next step asks for the matching credentials.

community.title: SNMP community
community.description: A community with read access. With v1 and v2c it travels in clear text.

data_description.community: The community with read access from the switch (SNMP → Community).

auth.title: SNMPv3 user
auth.description: The user must exist at the switch. Keys have at least 8 characters.

data_description.username: The SNMPv3 user from the switch.
data_description.auth_protocol: How the user logs in. "None" also switches encryption off.
data_description.auth_key: The password for authentication, at least 8 characters.
data_description.priv_protocol: How the traffic is encrypted. It needs authentication.
data_description.priv_key: The password for encryption, at least 8 characters.

error.cannot_connect: The switch does not answer. Check the address, the credentials and that SNMP is switched on and saved at the switch.
error.key_too_short: A key has at least 8 characters.
error.privacy_needs_authentication: Encryption only works together with authentication.

abort.already_configured: This switch is already set up.
abort.wrong_device: A different switch answers at this address.

init.title: Settings
init.description: How often Home Assistant asks the switch. Shorter intervals give more precise rates but put more load on the switch.

data_description.trap_port: UDP port on which Home Assistant receives SNMP traps from the switch (v1 and v2c only). At the switch under SNMP → Notification, add this machine with the port and the same community as a target, and Home Assistant shows a link change at once. Ports below 1024 need privileges; in Docker the UDP port must be published.
